subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Recovery, Sleep, Hydration, and Injury Prevention
title: Guided practice A: hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts
focus: hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts
essentialQuestion: Why does what I do between sessions decide what happens in them?
privacySafeScenario: Build a recovery protocol for the learner’s own program, including the specific signals that will trigger a reduced or rest day, and a graded return-to-activity plan.
studentTask: Learner applies hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing a condition builds the protocol with guardian input around the constraints they already have.
extensionChallenge: Apply hydration and fuelling around activity, without diets or calorie counts under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
